18737.etyen:
Derived from fork (“large, heavily built person”), originally in the sense “large, heavily built girl or woman”. Through the base noun, from Old Norse forkr (“boathook; stake, pole”), itself borrowed from Latin furca (“fork, pitchfork; fork-shaped support or pole”). The further origin of the Latin word is uncertain.
Earlier lexicography was less certain: Ivar Aasen recorded fyrkje (“girl, woman”) and tentatively compared fark and furk, whereas modern Bokmål dictionaries specifically derive the word from fork.
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk førkje (“girl, woman”) and dialectal Swedish Swedish förkje
